feed.title: antxiko — commented disassemblies of 8-bit games
feed.subtitle: Old 8-bit binaries taken apart byte by byte and commented, with the tools to rebuild them: nothing gets claimed that the binary does not show, and the source has to give the original back, byte for byte. Right now that means 64 MSX games.

entry.title: The Treasure of Usas: the music, taken from its engine and checked against openMSX
entry.summary: Every tune in the cartridge, made by running its own bank 13 sound engine frame by frame; the PSG writes match openMSX in every frame checked. And a finding: each ruin's tune changes with the mood of whoever goes in, up to two semitones higher or lower and with another instrument. 32 pieces to listen to.

entry.title: The Treasure of Usas: five ruins and four moods, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1987 MSX2 cartridge, 100% explained and commented to 40.1%. The 20 stages with their enemies, traps and items, the antechambers, the outside map, the bosses, Wit and Cles with their faces drawn from the ROM. What each mood changes, read in the code: a double jump, walking on thin air, the shot and the blow. And what four other Konami cartridges give in the other slot.

entry.title: Nemesis 2: twelve stages, five bosses and the cartridge next door, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1987 MSX cartridge with SCC, 100% explained and commented to 43.4%. The twelve stages, the five bosses, the 65 enemy types, the ship and the seven captured weapons drawn from the ROM. And what the cartridge in the other slot changes: three words in the pause with Q*bert, the equipment kept with The Maze of Galious, a penguin ship with Penguin Adventure; three secret stages and the way back.

entry.title: Metal Gear: all of Outer Heaven from its tables, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1987 MSX2 cartridge, 100% explained and commented to 46.8%. The 235 rooms in 9 zones with their lifts and doors, Snake, the 64 actor types, Metal Gear and the Hind D drawn from the ROM; the rooms match Manuel Pazos's reference images, thank you, Manuel. And five passwords in the pause, tape saving, what each item does and the order of the sixteen bombs.

entry.title: Konami's Synthesizer: a synthesizer inside the Z80, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1986 cartridge is not a game: it computes every note sample by sample and plays it through an 8-bit DAC. 100% explained and commented to 43.6%; the seven screens and the sixteen TONE EDITs drawn from the ROM and checked against openMSX, the engine written anew byte for byte, the pitch as a loop of cycles, the noise from the BIOS, and the tape of seven SAMPs that came with it.

entry.title: Rastan Saga: seven rounds, 255 screens and a dragon that is skipped, taken apart
entry.summary: Taito's 1988 MSX2 cartridge, 100% explained and commented to 46.1%. The seven rounds with their enemies and bosses, Rastan in his three layers and the 37 actor types, drawn from the ROM and checked against openMSX; plus the dragon stage the game skips, an ending it never draws and a test cheat in the header.

entry.title: The Maze of Galious on the Yamanooto: ESC leaves the load menu
entry.summary: With no slot saved there was no way out of the load menu but switching off (reported on real hardware). Now ESC goes back to the title, in the original and the Enhanced, also in nPackR 1.7.5.

entry.title: The Maze of Galious Enhanced also saves on the Yamanooto
entry.summary: bladeba's Enhanced (MSX2) gets the same three save slots in the cartridge's flash, on its own or inside nPackR 1.7.4. Both patches now come as IPS too.

entry.title: The front page, by sections: utilities, games and MSXon
entry.summary: Each section has its own page. In come nPackR, openMSXnet, msx-net-transfer, mHEXditor, MSXJuanEditor, RoOmSniFfeR, MORSE328p, Tiny Tetris VS, Tetris GG, OpenComputerFutbolSimulator, MysticBBSGames and MSXon.

entry.title: nPackR 1.7.3: The Maze of Galious saves to the flash
entry.summary: The GUI patches Galious when you drop it in, like the Metal Gears: three save slots in the cartridge's flash instead of the password.

entry.title: The Maze of Galious on the Yamanooto, tested on a real MSX
entry.summary: pabibiris tested the save patch on a real MSX with a real Yamanooto and approves it.

entry.title: The Yamanooto patches boot on their own, with no menu
entry.summary: The image each one builds no longer carries nPackR's menu: the game goes at the start of the flash and boots straight away. Galious and Metal Gear now switch banks through the Konami SCC registers, the mode a Yamanooto starts in.

entry.title: Saves on the Yamanooto: Galious, Metal Gear and Metal Gear 2
entry.summary: Three patches that save the game to the cartridge’s flash instead of to a password, a tape or the Game Master 2. Each one builds, from your own ROM, the image ready to flash.

entry.title: The Maze of Galious: the castle, ten worlds and 321 rooms, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1987 MSX cartridge (Knightmare II), 100% explained and commented to 40.1%. All 321 rooms laid out by their neighbours, the ten bosses, Popolon and Aphrodite, the items and the shops, drawn from the ROM and checked against openMSX down to zero; plus ZEUS in the pause, the cup on F2 and the black rooms that are hints and shops.
